$comment: GENERATED by `oxabl schema` from the oxabl config structs — DO NOT EDIT. Regenerate with `cargo run -p oxabl -- schema`.

idle_timeout.description: A fetch with no progress for this long ends. Default `30s`.

local.description: Host path of the shared local cache. Empty means the user cache directory.

local_job_dir.description: The per-job local cache directory of the `ci` and `read-only` modes.

local_max_size.description: Eviction limit of the local cache. Default `20GiB`.

remote.description: Use the remote cache. Default: whether `.oxabl/cache.toml` exists.

exclude.description: Glob patterns, relative to the root, of files that are not compile units. `**` crosses directories; a pattern that matches a directory excludes every file under it.

external_packages.description: Class name prefix to the library entries that supply it.

libraries.description: Procedure libraries outside the root and outside `$DLC`: a logical name and the path of the library as the worker sees it.

output.description: R-code output directory, under the workspace root. Required to compile.

outputs.description: Directories for the optional compiler outputs.

state.description: State directory, under the workspace root. Default `.oxabl/build`.

store.description: Host directory that holds `state.db` alone, for a root on a network file system. Empty keeps it in `state`.

verify.description: Verification of what a compile read.

BuildOutputs.description: The `[build.outputs]` table. An empty directory turns the output off.

batch_interval.description: Longest time a unit waits for the schema check. Default `60s`.

batch_units.description: Units held for the schema check that release them to a cache. Default 500.

reads.description: Read the compiler's own list of opened files and check it. Without it no cache write happens.

cancel_grace.description: Time for busy workers after a cancel. Default `30s`.

command.description: The argument list that starts one worker. Empty means unset.

count.description: Number of workers. Default: the CPU count, at most 8.

env.description: Extra environment variables for the command. Never a secret.

root.description: The workspace root as the worker sees it. Default: the host root.

LintConfig.description:
The `[workspace.lint]` table: which rule groups run, per-rule severities, and per-directory overrides.

Precedence, lowest first: each rule's default, then this table, then every override whose `files` match, in file order — a later override wins over an earlier one, so list broad patterns before narrow ones. Within one table a rule's own setting beats a group toggle, and `disable` beats `enable`. A group toggle turns rules on or off but keeps the severity an earlier table chose.

A group toggle in an override replaces an explicit setting for a rule in `[workspace.lint]` (an override is more specific than the global table), but not one made by the same or an earlier override: overrides rank equal, so a rule's own setting there stands against any later group toggle. A later rule setting always wins. For example, with `CL001 = "off"` in `[workspace.lint]`, an override that enables `strict.calls` turns `CL001` on for its files; with `CL001 = "off"` in an override for `a/**`, a later override for `**/*.p` that enables `strict.calls` leaves `CL001` off.

An override with no `files` patterns, or only invalid ones, applies to no file and is reported as a warning.

The `default` group (the `LINT` rules) is always on: it cannot be toggled as a group, but each of its rules can be set to `off`. The `strict.*` groups are off until enabled.

disable.description: Rule groups to turn off. Applied after `enable` in the same table.

enable.description: Rule groups to turn on, for example `["strict.calls"]`. A dotted prefix selects every group under it: `"strict"` turns on every `strict.*` group.

overrides.description: Per-directory or per-file settings, applied in order after the global ones.

LintOverride.description: One `[[workspace.lint.overrides]]` entry: settings for the files that match `files`. An entry with no `files` applies to nothing.

disable.description: Rule groups to turn off. Applied after `enable` in the same table.

enable.description: Rule groups to turn on, for example `["strict.calls"]`. A dotted prefix selects every group under it: `"strict"` turns on every `strict.*` group.

files.description: Glob patterns relative to the directory holding `oxabl.toml`, written with `/` and matched case-insensitively. `*` stays inside one directory, `**` crosses directories, and a pattern that matches a directory selects every file under it.

LintSeverity.description: Severity of a lint rule; `off` disables it.

PreprocessorConfig.description:
The `[workspace.preprocessor]` table: the compile environment behind the AVM's predefined preprocessor names.

The AVM answers `{&OPSYS}`, `{&WINDOW-SYSTEM}`, `{&BATCH-MODE}`, `{&PROCESS-ARCHITECTURE}` and `{&PROVERSION}` from the machine it compiles on. A static analyzer has no such machine, so the environment is stated here and every `&IF` over one of these names is decided against it. The defaults describe a 64-bit Unix batch compile with a character (TTY) UI; set the keys to describe the environment your code is really compiled in.

`{&FILE-NAME}`, `{&LINE-NUMBER}` and `{&SEQUENCE}` are computed from the source and take no configuration.

The `DBTYPE`, `CONNECTED` and `LDBNAME` functions of an `&IF` ask which databases are connected, which only a compile knows. `databases` states them; without it the `[workspace.schema]` file names stand in, as a partial list.

Container-level `#[serde(default)]` lets a partial table fall back per key, and `deny_unknown_fields` makes a misspelled key a hard error rather than a silently wrong branch.

batch-mode.description: Whether the compile is a batch compile; `{&BATCH-MODE}` expands to `yes` or `no`. Default `true`.

database-types.description: The `DBTYPE` of a connected database, by logical name, for example `{ ledger = "ORACLE" }`. A database that is not named here is `PROGRESS`.

databases.description:
The logical names of the databases connected when the code compiles, in the order of connection. The `DBTYPE`, `CONNECTED` and `LDBNAME` functions of an `&IF` answer from this list, so `DBTYPE("ledger") NE ?` is true when `ledger` is listed. The list is complete: a name that is not in it is not connected, so `DBTYPE` answers `?` and `CONNECTED` answers false. Use `[]` for a compile with no database connected. `DICTDB`, the alias the AVM gives the first connected database, answers as the first name in the list.

When the key is absent, the `[workspace.schema]` files name the databases: the file name without `.df` is the logical name, so `schema/ledger.df` connects `ledger`. A file name can differ from the logical name, and the files are in the order of `[workspace.schema]`, not of connection. So this list is not complete and not ordered: a name that is not in it raises `PREPROC010` instead of deciding that the database is absent, and so do `LDBNAME("DICTDB")` and `DBTYPE("DICTDB")`. `CONNECTED("DICTDB")` is true when the list is not empty. Set the key when a logical name differs from its file name. While neither a list nor a schema is given, an `&IF` that calls one of these functions raises `PREPROC010` instead of deciding on a guess.

proversion.description: Value of `{&PROVERSION}` and of the `PROVERSION` function, for example `"12.8"`. There is no default: the version is not something a tool can guess. While it is unset, an `&IF` condition that reads either form raises `PREPROC009` instead of silently deciding against an empty string.

Size.description: An integer and a unit: `KiB`, `MiB`, `GiB` or `TiB`.

SourceEncoding.description:
The character encoding of ABL source files on disk (`[workspace.sources].encoding`).

Every encoding decodes to the same Unicode text in memory; spans and offsets the tools report are byte offsets into that text.

oneOf.description: UTF-8. A file with invalid UTF-8 cannot be read.
ISO 8859-1 (Latin-1): every byte is the code point of the same value.
Windows code page 1252. Every byte decodes; the five bytes the code page leaves undefined (0x81, 0x8D, 0x8F, 0x90, 0x9D) become the C1 control of the same value.

case_insensitive_lookup.description:
When a class or `RUN` target is not found under the spelling the source used or its lower-case fold, look for a file whose path matches ignoring case. Default `false`.

Meant for a case-sensitive filesystem holding a tree written for a case-insensitive one (`RUN Sub/Prog.p` stored as `sub/prog.p`). It lists directories on every miss, so it costs more than the default lookup. Two distinct matches still leave the name unresolved.

directories.description: Directories to walk for ABL *root* files — `.p`, `.w`, `.cls`, and `.v`, matched case-insensitively. `.i` is deliberately not among them: an include fragment is never a root, and `is_root_file` is the one policy that decides.

dlc.description: The host directory that holds the include sources of the OpenEdge installation the workers use. Machine-specific, so usually set through `OXABL_DLC_SOURCES`, which overrides it. Without either, the includes under a `$DLC/` entry do not resolve.

encoding.description:
The character encoding of source files: `"utf-8"` (the default), `"iso-8859-1"` or `"windows-1252"`. `"utf8"`, `"latin1"` and `"cp1252"` are accepted as aliases.

It applies to every file read from disk: roots, include files, classes and `.df` schema files, and `oxabl format` writes a file back in the same encoding. A UTF-8 byte order mark always means UTF-8 and is removed, whatever this says. `"utf-8"` rejects a file with invalid UTF-8; see `fallback_encoding`.

fallback_encoding.description:
The encoding to use for a file that is not valid UTF-8. Unset by default, so such a file cannot be read.

For a tree that mixes UTF-8 files and single-byte ones. It only matters when `encoding` is `"utf-8"`: a single-byte encoding decodes every file.

include_paths.description:
Include search paths, searched in order (PROPATH equivalent).

An entry that starts with `$DLC/` (or is `$DLC`) names a directory under [`dlc`](Self::dlc). An entry `$LIB:<name>` names a procedure library of `[build.libraries]`; it holds r-code, so the analysis does not search it.

root_extensions.description:
Extensions that make a file an ABL *root* when a directory is walked, written without the dot and matched case-insensitively. Default `["p", "w", "cls", "v"]`.

Use it for shop conventions such as `.pp` or `.cgi`. It decides which files `oxabl check` and the other directory walks pick up; a file named on the command line is always accepted. A leading dot is ignored. An entry that is empty, holds a path separator, or is `i` is dropped with a warning: an include fragment is never a root. The list replaces the default, so keep the defaults you still need.

root_relative_include_paths.description:
Search paths resolved against the directory of each root file and searched before `include_paths`, in order. Default empty.

For a shop that compiles each program with its own directory, or fixed subdirectories of it, first on the PROPATH: `[".", "rf"]` searches `<dir>` and `<dir>/rf` for a root in `<dir>`. Includes, classes and `RUN` targets are all searched this way; an indexed class or program reads its own includes with the paths of its own directory.

run_extensions.description:
Extensions tried, in order, for a `RUN` target written without one (`RUN post-order`), written without the dot. Default `["p", "w"]`.

A leading dot is ignored, and an entry that is empty or holds a path separator is dropped with a warning. Each extension is tried as written and then in lower case, against the name as written and then folded.

The first extension that finds a file wins. A list that omits an extension never links a bare name to such a file; an empty list links no bare name at all.

StyleGuide.description:
Comprehensive ABL style guide holding all formatting and diagnostic rules.

The struct uses `#[serde(default)]` so partial TOML files work: any missing field falls back to `Default::default()` which delegates to [`StyleGuide::default_base`]. It also uses `deny_unknown_fields` so a misspelled or unrecognized rule key is a hard error rather than being silently ignored — the config is user-facing, so a typo must fail loudly.

max_consecutive_blank_lines.description: Maximum number of consecutive blank lines the formatter permits before collapsing the run (and trimming file edges).

TimeSpan.description: An integer and a unit: `s`, `m` or `h`.

lint.description: Lint rule groups, severities and per-directory overrides (`[workspace.lint]`).

preprocessor.description: The compile environment the preprocessor reports through its predefined names (`[workspace.preprocessor]`).

sources.description: Source file locations and include paths.

style.description:
Formatter style rules (`[workspace.style]`).

Embeds [`StyleGuide`] directly (no wrapper type): it already derives `Deserialize` with `#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]`, so a partial table fills unspecified fields from [`StyleGuide::default_base`], an absent section yields `default_base()`, and an unknown key is a hard parse error.

XrefFormat.description: The form of the cross-reference output.

description:
Top-level configuration deserialized from `oxabl.toml`.

An unknown top-level table is an error, so a misspelled `[biuld]` is not a silent no-op.

build.description: How `oxabl build` keeps state and compiles (`[build]`).
